answer: Picture the network as a garden where each new agent must tend one plot for several epochs before it can harvest. Rewards vest slowly, so a farmer who plants a hundred fake identities waits just as long for each one while paying their upkeep up front. Graders then act like a prism, splitting answers by style and timing; clusters that bend the light the same way get flagged for review. Saffron is costly because the crocus grows slowly and must be picked by hand, and a sybil should be just as costly.
